blocks.text: Meta updates are something we can’t influence but have to adapt to. We had an in-depth conversation with support, during which we learned about several updates that are already affecting our work. Here are the key points.

A geo-targeting update is coming. If the announcement is to be believed, the ability to exclude individual geo zones, cities or districts at the campaign level will be removed — instead, you’ll be able to exclude them at the account level. We’ll see how this works in practice.
What this means for your work: if your campaigns use precise regional exclusions, prepare a plan B — the structure will have to be rebuilt one level up.

This recommendation isn’t the most obvious, but according to the marketing team, to take part in the auction properly, budgets today need to be adjusted by +25%. Roughly speaking, if you have a $100 budget, add $25, for a total of $125.
Seven days for testing and stabilization

This isn’t about learning but specifically about testing and stabilization — seven days are allotted for it. It’s good they said it directly: far too many people stop campaigns on day three without waiting for them to stabilize.
The creative recommendations are as expected. As for the rejections everyone is seeing right now, there is a specific procedure for handling them, and support confirms this.
What to do with this information

items: Review the structure of campaigns where geographic exclusions are set precisely
Keep a budget reserve when planning — the auction demands more than it seems
Don’t stop tests before seven days: results before then aren’t representative
